Today's TL;DRRegimeMIXED
Markets are in a MIXED regime as an unprecedented US economic escalation against Iran and Strait of Hormuz blockade — combined with NATO-Russia drone incidents and US fiscal deterioration — creates a powerful geopolitical risk-off anchor, while sticky-but-not-surging US inflation data, resilient global demand, AI infrastructure financing booms, and consumer strength support risk-on pockets. The net effect is a bifurcated market where energy, defense, and cyber-security assets rally, but trade-sensitive cyclicals, long-duration bonds, and EM FX face headwinds from the Iran conflict and fiscal stress.

Memory and semiconductor pricing upcycle内存与半导体定价上升周期
×8 · 31 steps
Memory and semiconductor supply-demand tightness is driving a pricing upcycle that is broadening beyond memory: AI and data-center demand have pushed DRAM ASPs +275% Y/Y, NAND +368% Y/Y, and June memory revenue to $88.4B. The recovery is now spreading to analog, power, and MCU segments, with ex-memory sales rising to $63.5B (+38% Y/Y), analog above trendline, and power semi utilization/pricing strong. HBM shortages persist, forcing de-specification, while NAND eSSD TAM grows at mid-50% YoY.
16 extracted · 8 firms

BYD's flash-charging model ramp boosted domestic share back to 23% in March.

×9 · 35 steps
AI-related companies account for about 40% of US follow-on equity issuance YTD, and more are expected to raise capital. Goldman Sachs lifts Tencent's 2026-28E capex to Rmb210bn/245bn/247bn, with 2Q26 capex payments of. Despite massive capex increases (TSMC $60-64bn, Intel >$20bn) and rising leverage, hyperscalers have meaningful headroom to fund further expansion without materially diluting ROIC (19-17% under stress scenarios). HSBC dismisses concerns about funding constraints slowing AI infrastructure build-out.

AI hardware supply constraints and pricing powerAI硬件供应约束与定价权
×5 · 20 steps
AI server component pricing and margins are rising on rising complexity. AVC's GM rose to 32.6% (from 24.4% a year ago) driven by higher-margin liquid cooling components that carry increasing dollar content and complexity. AVC is benefiting from a transition to liquid cooling for AI GPUs and ASICs, with revenue growth accelerating in 2H26 (16% QoQ in 3Q26E expected). The company captures a wide share of the thermal BOM including cold plates, CDUs, and manifolds, supporting raised 2026-28E earnings by 5%/12%/18%.

Tencent is ramping AI compute infrastructure for Hy4 and Weixin AI agent Xiaowei, raising 2026-28E capex to Rmb200.7bn/235bn/220bn. Non-IFRS OP growth (5.8%/2.7%/8.5%) lags revenue growth (9.3%/9.1%/9%) due to AI spend, but management expects long-term payoffs via higher-margin cloud and productivity AI tools like WorkBuddy.

    Premise开源模型带来定价竞争

    Open-weight models create pricing competition across the model layer; the firm has already seen multiple U.S. labs release lower-priced offerings (Meta's Muse Spark 1.2 released last week) and views lower token pricing (open weight, lower cost near frontier models) as translating to lower incremental unit economics for model providers, putting higher importance on token throughput, adoption and building an ecosystem (similar to other open builds like Android).
    132c91df32af·《How Could Open-Weight Models Impact GenAI ROIC?》·2026-08-13
  2. 2
    Mechanism硬件架构提升token吞吐
    Token throughput is a critical input to revenue/GW at the model layer; improvements come from 1) better hardware (more memory capacity at chip level and rack level) and faster interconnects, 2) model
    Token throughput is a critical input to revenue/GW at the model layer; improvements come from 1) better hardware (more memory capacity at chip level and rack level) and faster interconnects, 2) model architecture improvements increasing model sparsity within MoE models (active parameters/total parameters), 3) software improvements from request batching, and 4) hyperscaler-specific gains from proprietary hardware (custom silicon via TPUs/Trainium) and software (hyperscalers have the deepest enterprise footprints and thus the highest volume of requests to batch); higher token throughput directly corresponds to better revenue/GW at the model layer and hyperscalers' ability to drive throughput is directly supportive of their own economics through durable GPU rental pricing.
    132c91df32af·《How Could Open-Weight Models Impact GenAI ROIC?》·2026-08-13
  3. 3
    Mechanism超大规模云商多重变现路径
    Hyperscaler monetization paths on open weights include 1) serverless API token revenue (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex), 2) accelerator rental revenue (customers self-deploying need dedicated GPU capacity),
    Hyperscaler monetization paths on open weights include 1) serverless API token revenue (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex), 2) accelerator rental revenue (customers self-deploying need dedicated GPU capacity), 3) RAG (connecting open models to proprietary data, driving storage and database revenue), and 4) security (governance, guardrails, identity, monitoring); API token revenue on open models may be a loss leader (like milk in a grocery store) while open models have the potential to generate more core cloud infrastructure attach per workload.
    132c91df32af·《How Could Open-Weight Models Impact GenAI ROIC?》·2026-08-13
  4. 4
    Conclusion超大规模云商单位经济仍吸引
    Four reasons hyperscalers' unit economics will remain attractive even hosting lower-cost open-weight models: 1) compute is the scarce resource enterprises rely on hyperscalers to provide; 2) hyperscal
    Four reasons hyperscalers' unit economics will remain attractive even hosting lower-cost open-weight models: 1) compute is the scarce resource enterprises rely on hyperscalers to provide; 2) hyperscalers will continue to monetize multi-billion dollar compute investments to maximize ROIC, with more volume at lower per-token or GW unit economics meaning EBIT dollar growth matters more than percentage margins; 3) hyperscalers and model developers will remain highly focused on token throughput; 4) all GenAI workloads will drive attach of other services and incremental profitability — compute is the scarce and expensive resource hyperscalers will rationally monetize, and remaining the lower-cost provider of compute (via improving token throughput) will likely remain critical.

Trump Admin Escalates Trade War: De Minimis Loophole Closed & Drone Tariffs Imposed
A US Court of International Trade upheld the Trump administration's authority to close the $800 de minimis tariff loophole, ending duty-free entry for low-value packages and raising compliance costs for e-commerce importers. Simultaneously, the administration invoked Section 232 to impose tariffs up to 100% on imported drones and components, citing national security. This dual action intensifies trade tensions with China and raises input costs for cross-border e-commerce, retail platforms, and drone-dependent industries.

    Token throughput is a critical input to revenue/GW at the model layer; improvements come from 1) better hardware (more memory capacity at chip level and rack level) and faster interconnects, 2) model architecture improvements increasing model sparsity within MoE models (active parameters/total parameters), 3) software improvements from request batching, and 4) hyperscaler-specific gains from proprietary hardware (custom silicon via TPUs/Trainium) and software (hyperscalers have the deepest enterprise footprints and thus the highest volume of requests to batch); higher token throughput directly corresponds to better revenue/GW at the model layer and hyperscalers' ability to drive throughput is directly supportive of their own economics through durable GPU rental pricing.

    Hyperscaler monetization paths on open weights include 1) serverless API token revenue (Bedrock, Foundry, Vertex), 2) accelerator rental revenue (customers self-deploying need dedicated GPU capacity), 3) RAG (connecting open models to proprietary data, driving storage and database revenue), and 4) security (governance, guardrails, identity, monitoring); API token revenue on open models may be a loss leader (like milk in a grocery store) while open models have the potential to generate more core cloud infrastructure attach per workload.

    Four reasons hyperscalers' unit economics will remain attractive even hosting lower-cost open-weight models: 1) compute is the scarce resource enterprises rely on hyperscalers to provide; 2) hyperscalers will continue to monetize multi-billion dollar compute investments to maximize ROIC, with more volume at lower per-token or GW unit economics meaning EBIT dollar growth matters more than percentage margins; 3) hyperscalers and model developers will remain highly focused on token throughput; 4) all GenAI workloads will drive attach of other services and incremental profitability — compute is the scarce and expensive resource hyperscalers will rationally monetize, and remaining the lower-cost provider of compute (via improving token throughput) will likely remain critical.
